mfg1-electrical-weekly-07-q01.stem: A practice result is theory 21/30 and practical 5/10. How is it assessed using this app’s equally weighted practice questions?
options: Both pass because the total is 26/40.
Theory meets its threshold; practical does not.
Surplus theory answers can cover practical.
Neither can be assessed from correct counts.
reasons: Separate thresholds cannot be replaced by a combined score.
Compare theory’s minimum 20 and practical’s minimum 6 separately.
Correct answers cannot transfer between sections.
This textbook specifies separate minimum counts.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-07-q02.stem: You hear unusual vibration from a panel outside your responsibility. Which response fits your role?
options: Touch the energized interior to investigate.
Hide the discovery if the noise stops.
Make the situation safe under the approved procedure and report the equipment and observations.
A safety manager means workers need not report.
reasons: Unauthorized contact with energized parts is dangerous.
Information remains necessary even if it temporarily stops.
Respect roles and report observed facts.
Management arrangements do not replace individual reporting.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-07-q03.stem: A terminal shelf has 5 against a lower limit of 8, and one wrong part. What should you do?
options: Move everything to another empty shelf.
The three fixed conditions concern location only.
Count the wrong item as specified stock.
Identify and report shortage and mixing separately after checking.
reasons: Moving alone resolves neither cause nor identity.
Item and quantity are also included.
A wrong item is not stock of the specified part.
Check deviations in both item and quantity.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-07-q04.stem: You only watched a demonstration during OJT on a new machine. What must be checked before assignment?
options: One pair of gloves for all tasks is enough.
Required education/qualifications, authorization scope, and understood procedures.
reasons: OJT does not automatically replace qualifications.
Gloves can be hazardous around rotation.
OJT, requirements, and understanding are separate checks.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-07-q05.stem: A site has signs for an evacuation building and a tsunami refuge. How do you choose?
options: Match disaster type with the workplace evacuation plan.
Both are always equivalent if green.
Evacuation locations are unnecessary if prohibitions are obeyed.
reasons: Location purpose and disaster conditions differ.
The same color does not establish the same target.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-07-q06.stem: A decanted cleaning liquid has no known product name, and the original container is missing. First response?
options: Smell a little to identify it.
Suspend use and ask for product identification and SDS confirmation.
Mix it if the color matches the old liquid.
reasons: Identify first, then match hazard information.
A missing label is not evidence of safety.
Color does not establish composition or compatibility.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-07-q07.stem: A part nearly fell this month without injury. How should 1:29:300 be used?
options: Serious accidents cannot occur before 300 events.
Treat it as a warning, report it, and assess measures; do not use counts as safety limits.
reasons: No count guarantees safety before it.
The ratio is a concept, not a predictive guarantee.
A count ratio cannot establish cause.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-07-q08.stem: For a 65% threshold on 30 theory questions, what is the minimum correct count?
reasons: At least 19.5 means 20 as an integer.
Do not calculate using 40 combined questions.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-07-q09.stem: Shelf location and part number are right but stock exceeds the specified upper limit. Which condition is primarily violated?

mfg1-electrical-weekly-07-q10.stem: Is it acceptable to test a rotating machine before training because you have protective glasses?
options: No: protection, education, and authorization are separate checks.
Yes: protecting the eyes removes every hazard.
New work needs no startup check.
reasons: Several safety conditions must be met.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-07-q11.stem: Before reading an SDS, what information should first match?
options: Product identification on the container and SDS.
reasons: Color does not identify the product.
Different contents can use similar containers.
Another product’s SDS can have different requirements.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-07-q12.stem: New trip hazards increase a week after a safety measure. What is the OSHMS response?
options: Stop observing because implementation is complete.
Assess new risks and effectiveness, then revise the plan.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-08-q01.stem: Material lot and tool changed when defects increased. What should quality investigation do?
options: Compare facts through 4M, including material and machine changes.
Treat design and logistics quality as identical.
reasons: Do not lower safety or quality requirements.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-08-q02.stem: With matched inspection conditions, defects changed from 6/200 to 2/200. Which explanation is correct?
options: Always touch energized items for actual-item checks.
The rate fell from 3%to 1%; assess other conditions too.
reasons: The three actuals do not require dangerous touching.
Keep the denominator and other conditions in the assessment.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-08-q03.stem: A drawing is revised but the QC process chart is old. What before starting?
options: Resolve the target/revision mismatch and align approved control conditions.
A work standard makes QC conditions unnecessary.
Hide the old version and record it as new.
reasons: Instructions and controls have different roles.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-08-q04.stem: A scatterplot shows larger dimensions at higher temperatures. What can currently be said?
options: A relationship is observed; other conditions need checking before deciding cause.
Temperature alone is proven the sole cause.
A scatterplot is a time-series control-limit chart.
Correlation removes the need for data counts.
reasons: Conditions and sample size remain necessary.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-08-q05.stem: A dropped instrument has a JIS mark. How should its next use be decided?
options: Organizational ISO certification automatically passes each result.
JIS and product inspection mean the same thing.
Check condition, calibration, and pre-use requirements, not the mark alone.
reasons: Certification scope differs from individual results.
Standards conformity differs from inspection of the item.
Marking and present reliability are separate.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-08-q06.stem: What is the calculated energy for 900 W used 20 minutes?
reasons: Minutes were used directly as hours.
The duration is not one hour.
W is not an energy unit.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-08-q07.stem: Equal-volume reference water has mass 40 g; material specific gravity is 2.7. What is its calculated mass?
reasons: Specific gravity cannot be added to mass.
The equal-volume water mass was not multiplied.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-08-q08.stem: Drawing requirements were met but delivery was late. How should customer requirements be considered?
options: Check both quality characteristics and delivery timing.
Delivery is not part of QCD.
Logistics has no relation to quality.
reasons: This ignores the commitment to the customer.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-08-q09.stem: Which PDCA stage compares target and actual result?
reasons: It feeds evaluated results into improvement.
It evaluates results against the target.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-08-q10.stem: A worker independently changed “once per lot” to “once per hour.” What is the problem?
options: Both always inspect the same quantity.
Equal wording length means equivalent conditions.
Control conditions were substituted without approval.
reasons: Text length is not a control condition.
Time and lots are different divisions.
Frequency is an important control item.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-08-q11.stem: “Tool wear” is written on a 4Mcause-and-effect diagram. What is its current status?
reasons: Writing it does not prove it.
It is not a numerical relationship coefficient.
A length factor was directly used for area.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-09-q01.stem: How do returnable-box reuse and copper-offcut recovery differ?
options: The first is Reuse, the second Recycle.
Both only aim to increase waste.
Recycling needs no separation or identification.
reasons: Distinguish using a product again from recovering resources.
Resource recovery such as melting is different.
Different materials and hazards need sorting.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-09-q02.stem: You want an unknown-specification AC adapter in a panel. How should checks be divided?
options: Old product counts establish current coverage.
Check product coverage, installation suitability, and worker conditions separately.
reasons: A mark does not establish every use.
Do not decide omission conditions independently.
Check the applicable date and public guidance.
Product, installation, and work requirements are separate.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-09-q03.stem: An export specification states an IEC edition. How should a domestic part be chosen?
options: Any JIS in that field is automatically identical.
Even corresponding JIS requires checking editions, differences, and contractual requirements.
reasons: Editions and national differences can exist.
Number, edition, and scope are needed.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-09-q04.stem: In third-angle projection, where is the right-side view relative to the front?
reasons: Views are placed on their corresponding viewing side.
Below is for the bottom view, not the standard right-side location.
The title block identifies the drawing.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-09-q05.stem: A20.02 mm hole and 19.98 mm shaft give what dimensional difference?
reasons: This ignores actual dimensions and limits.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-09-q06.stem: Coil and contacts with device identifier M are on different sheets. How do you read them?
options: Associate them only with the nearest coil.
Use identifiers and cross-references and track states.
Ladder instructions are always literal wiring pictures.
reasons: Expanded drawings can separate parts of one device.
Separate logical conditions from actual wiring.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-09-q07.stem: You read insulation classF155°C. Which decision is appropriate?
options: Use natural rubber as inorganic material.
Aluminum is an insulator because magnets scarcely attract it.
Check insulation-system conditions and product specifications rather than treating it as ambient temperature.
reasons: This is not every product’s ambient rating.
Class scope and use conditions are needed.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-09-q08.stem: Current retains direction while changing magnitude. What can be said from direction?
options: DC must be the same magnitude at all times.
It can be treated as DC despite varying magnitude.
Direction has no relation to DC/AC.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-09-q09.stem: Someone will remove grounding based only on one line in an old textbook. What is appropriate?
options: A leakage breaker always permits removal.
Low voltage always makes it unnecessary.
Verify current applicability with the responsible person.
Cutting it with a marked tool is fine.
reasons: The two protections have different roles.
Omission depends on installation and legal applicability.
A tool mark is not installation authorization.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-09-q10.stem: You see JEM and JIS labels. Which identification is correct?
options: Both are laws of every country.
Compare content as standards with different issuers and scopes.
Similar letters prove the same document.
reasons: Standards and laws are not identical.
Names alone do not prove identity.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-09-q11.stem: Paper enlarged fromA4 toA3 but the dimension remains 45 mm. How do you read the product requirement?
options: Double to 90 mm with the paper.
reasons: Paper size is not product size.
Separate representation size from real dimensions.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-09-q12.stem: Ra 3.2 μm was issued as a 3.2 mm length instruction. What is the issue?
options: μm and mm have the same numerical meaning.
Roughness, length dimensions, and units were confused.
Roughness can be ignored even if specified.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-10-q01.stem: IV and KIV wires share a shelf. What before wiring?
options: Check structure, ratings, conductor area, destination, and specified part number.
Use mm and mm²as the same numbers.
A terminal fitting the screw removes wire compatibility needs.
reasons: Match actual specifications with instructions, not names alone.
The wire must also fit the terminal’s range.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-10-q02.stem: Flux changed to a different product. How do you decide residue treatment?
options: Soak all products in one solvent.
Check cleaning need and method through material specifications and approved processing.
All lead-free products are defective under every condition.
reasons: One appearance feature does not judge everything.
Alloy class alone does not determine quality.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-10-q03.stem: A fixed resistor looks like a thermistor. How do you decide interchangeability?
options: Same resistance now always means interchangeable.
Passive parts require no heat or charge precautions.
Compare temperature behavior, ratings, and purpose in documentation.
reasons: Terminal count alone does not determine function.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-10-q04.stem: A workpiece rotates while a fixed cutting tool machines its outside diameter. Which basic machine?
options: Every machine rotates only its cutter
reasons: What rotates depends on the machine.
It measures light; it is not a machine tool.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-10-q05.stem: Same material/temperature: length doubles and area triples. What is the resistance ratio?
reasons: Resistance follows length divided by area.
The length increase is handled backward.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-10-q06.stem: What is the period of 25 Hz in ms?
reasons: Frequency’s number was used as period.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-10-q07.stem: 18 V is applied to 40 Ωin series with 120 Ωparallel to 240 Ω. What is total current?
reasons: This treats all three as series.
The decimal point is one place wrong.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-10-q08.stem: Conductor area fits a terminal but its hole does not fit the mounting screw. What should you do?
options: Change to a thinner screw yourself.
Confirm the specified terminal fitting both wire and screw.
Enlarge the terminal hole without approval.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-10-q09.stem: A component was bent sharply immediately after soldering. What must be checked?
options: Inspect joint and land damage against criteria and obtain approved action.
Add much solder to fix everything.
reasons: Movement during cooling and force can cause defects.
Shine alone does not determine quality.
Quantity alone does not solve every defect.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-10-q10.stem: Which description fits an NC machine with automatic tool changing?
options: Lathes always rotate only the tool.
It is a characteristic of a machining center.
reasons: First-run checks and similar precautions remain needed.
Distinguish NC from the automatic-change feature.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-10-q11.stem: What is power for an ideal DC resistor at 24 V and 120 Ω?
reasons: Power without time integration is in W.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-10-q12.stem: In an ideal purely inductive sinusoidal circuit, how is current relative to voltage?
options: Exactly the same waveform at all times.
Voltage and current are the same quantity.
reasons: This is the ideal-inductor phase relation.
It differs from purely resistive in-phase behavior too.
They have different units and quantities.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-11-q01.stem: Which describes a pn-junction depletion layer?
options: A hole with no atoms or fixed charges.
Proof that all n-type material has net negative charge.
Exactly the same interior as metal wire.
A region with fewer mobile majority carriers and an internal field.
reasons: Semiconductor junctions have their own state.
Distinguish carriers from the junction field.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-11-q02.stem: Someone assumes a gate terminal has the same order as a BJT base. What is appropriate?
options: All three-terminal devices have the same layout.
Check FET or other type, terminals, drive, and ratings.
Use hFE to determine every device’s maximum voltage.
Select IGBT from package color alone.
reasons: Control and terminal roles vary by device.
A characteristic ratio does not replace maximum ratings.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-11-q03.stem: Full scale 100, indication 64, range 5 V: what is the reading?
reasons: Scale number was not converted to the range.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-11-q04.stem: Of 32 planned items,25 are complete,2 held, and 5 not started. How do you hand over?
options: Identify and record each state, quantity, and unfinished work.
Mix held items into good stock.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-11-q06.stem: Before replacing an SSR whose output is off, which understanding is correct?
options: Off means all terminals may be touched.
Check semiconductor leakage and remaining voltage through specifications and isolation procedures.
All SSRs fully open mechanical contacts.
A contactor always includes short-circuit protection.
reasons: Off indication does not prove no voltage.
Separate output method from safe isolation.
Load switching and short-circuit protection are different.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-11-q07.stem: A basic 3-second on-delay receives only 2 seconds of input. What happens?
options: It first turns on 3 seconds after input-off.
Input does not last long enough for output-on.
Every model self-holds even below the setting.
reasons: This confuses off-delay and also reverses output action.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-11-q08.stem: What is the majority carrier in p-type material?
reasons: Phosphorus is a donor example for n-type.
Holes are treated as the majority carriers in p-type.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-11-q09.stem: Match producing a periodic signal with retrieving a signal from a received wave.
options: Both are always power stabilization only.
reasons: They differ from supporting supply conditions.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-11-q10.stem: A DMM manual explicitly lists AC current. How does this relate to the textbook overview?
options: Ignore it and insist measurement is impossible.
Any capability means safe at every voltage.
Avoid a blanket claim; check this model’s terminals, ratings, and procedure.
reasons: Check model differences and meet safety conditions.
It does not match for all inputs.
De Morgan turns negated OR into AND of the negations.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-11-q12.stem: A basic off-delay input goes off at 4 seconds; its setting is 2 seconds. When does output go off?
reasons: Retention is separate from this basic behavior.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-12-q01.stem: What is synchronous rotating-field speed at 60 Hz and 6 poles?
options: The actual rotor is also always 1200 min⁻¹
reasons: Frequency is not multiplied by pole count.
A loaded induction rotor has slip.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-12-q02.stem: At unchanged winding resistance, current becomes 1.5 times as large. What is the copper-loss ratio?

mfg1-electrical-weekly-12-q03.stem: Appearance/function passed but a required humidity test is missing. What record is appropriate?
options: Use a multimeter to replace withstand-voltage and life tests.
Add the test without qualifications or approval.
Separate completed results from untested requirements.
reasons: Test purposes cannot substitute for one another.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-12-q04.stem: Compare 2 failures/100 hours and 3/300 hours. Per operating hour, which is right?
options: 3 failures always means a higher rate.
0.02/hour versus 0.01/hour, so the latter rate is lower.
Everything is equal unless zero failures.
reasons: Rates and effects must be distinguished.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-12-q05.stem: Express 3 events among 25000 shipments per million.
reasons: The proportion was not converted per million.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-12-q06.stem: Match the part pushing a molding out with the resin entrance to the product cavity.
options: Both always have the same shape for every product.
Draft has no relation to demolding.
reasons: Each mold/product needs its own design.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-12-q07.stem: Hardened negative resist remains over needed copper. What is primarily removed by copper etching?
reasons: Resist protects needed copper while unwanted copper is removed.
This differs from chemical pattern formation.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-12-q08.stem: At shaft speed 900 min⁻¹ and torque 4 N·m, what is approximate mechanical power?
reasons: Speed conversion and the coefficient are needed.
Power is in W, not accumulated energy.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-12-q09.stem: Gas-insulated equipment uses SF6. Which maintenance approach is appropriate?
options: Check environmental/safety information and approved recovery/handling.
Looking only at the low-voltage side removes all hazards.
reasons: Hazard and environmental effects are material-specific.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-12-q10.stem: Can a single startup replace accelerated life-test records?
options: Yes, one operation guarantees all lifetime.
No: reliability assessment with defined periods and conditions serves a different purpose.
All safety tests are identical too.
Pass it before carrying out the missing test.
reasons: It does not assess performance over time.
Required testing conditions must be met.
This falsifies result order and records.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-12-q11.stem: A do-not-stack package looks strong. What handling is correct?
options: Add two levels because it looks strong.
Follow marking/specification and put no other load above it.
reasons: Do not change protection requirements from appearance.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-12-q12.stem: Which correctly separates board layer count from form?
options: Multilayer describes structure; flexible describes form.
Bare and assembled boards are always at the same manufacturing stage.
reasons: Mounting components changes the manufacturing stage.
